title: Documentation Drift in AI-Generated Pull Requests
abstract: arXiv:2610.27381v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: AI coding agents now contribute to software repositories at scale, yet their documentation practices remain uncharacterised. We analyse 29,669 AI-generated pull requests from 2,585 repositories in the AIDev dataset, measuring documentation co-change: whether code-file modifications are accompanied by a documentation-file update in the same PR. We find that 63.2% of AI PRs change code without updating any documentation. This varies sharply by task type: 55.2% for features and 77.5% for refactoring. Undocumented code files are followed by a fix to the same file 8.6 to 11.7% more often than documented files across 30 to 90-day windows. A raw PR-level comparison shows the opposite because documented PRs are 3.9 times larger and therefore attract more fixes. Controlling for size exposure reverses this result. Documented changes also merge faster despite their larger size (median: 40 seconds versus 184 seconds), although merging is largely aut

translated_title: AI生成拉取请求中的文档漂移
translated_abstract: AI编程代理如今正大规模地为软件仓库做出贡献，但其文档编写实践仍未被系统性地刻画。我们分析了AIDev数据集中来自2,585个仓库的29,669个AI生成的拉取请求（PR），以衡量文档协同变更：即代码文件的修改是否在同一PR中伴随文档文件的更新。我们发现63.2%的AI PR在不更新任何文档的情况下修改代码，且这一比例因任务类型而有显著差异：功能开发类为55.2%，重构类为77.5%。在30至90天的时间窗口内，无文档代码文件随后对同一文件进行修复的概率比有文档文件高8.6%至11.7%。在PR层面的原始比较中结果相反，因为有文档的PR规模是无文档PR的3.9倍，因而吸引了更多修复；而在控制规模暴露因素后，这一结果被逆转。尽管规模更大，有文档的变更合并速度也更快（中位数：40秒对比184秒），尽管合并主要由自动……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该研究首次大规模刻画了AI生成代码的文档编写实践，发现63.2%的AI拉取请求在修改代码时不更新任何文档，且无文档的代码文件后续被修复的概率显著更高，揭示了“文档漂移”现象及其对软件质量的负面影响。
en_tdlr: This study provides the first large-scale characterization of documentation practices in AI-generated pull requests, finding that 63.2% of AI PRs modify code without updating documentation and that undocumented files are significantly more likely to require subsequent fixes, revealing a "documentation drift" phenomenon that harms software quality.
